new.st: Town platted 1856 by Thomas H. Forde and Judge Casey on the Mississippi shore at an old Dakota tepee village, 'four miles southeast of Wabasha'. 1857: three-story hotel, two stores, blacksmith shop, ~30 houses; Sinclair & Co. sawmill (30 men) from spring 1858. Boats stopped landing; the deserted buildings were burned by an incendiary one March night in 1859. 'No trace of it can now be seen' (1884).
new.t: Pin is the stated distance from Wabasha only (4 mi SE, on the shore at Sand Prairie). Needs a plat or GLO note for the section. Single source, C.

new.st: Defunct village laid out 1863 by William A. Johnson on 40 acres, NW1/4 sec. 27, on Orin Hancock's claim (Hancock hotel on sec. 22, 1857; post office 1862; store 1862, later Henry Etting). The railroad went farther east (Kellogg), and by 1884 only three or four houses marked the 'ancient site of Pauselim'.

new.n: Brink's tavern / 'the Burnt Tavern', West Albany (1855)
new.st: Samuel Brink built a two-story log hotel 24x46 ft on the SW1/4 of sec. 21 in June 1855, the first building in West Albany township; it burned the next summer while Frederick Jacobs had it, and the settlement was called 'the Burnt Tavern' for some time. First road through: Read's Landing to Oronoco and Mazeppa via West Albany.

t-pan-zumbro-sluice.st: 1884 county history: the Oronoco Mining Company (fall 1858) set its sluices on sec. 22 of Mazeppa township (T109N R14W, centre about 44.2309,-92.4812) in a clay bank in the narrow valley that gave 'shot gold'. Spring 1859 high water took the first works; the rebuilt works cleaned up a little over $20 on their first Saturday and were swept away by the flood of 3 July 1859, ending the work. Ground check: consider moving this pin to sec. 22. Geology of Minnesota (1888) also names secs. 6 and 27 of Mazeppa for gold washed from the drift, and says gold occurs along the Zumbro from Rochester and Oronoco to the Wabasha border, mostly in the stream bed.

vs-2064578.st: 1884: West Albany village grew around Richard Dawson's hotel, Applegarth's gristmill, McIntyre's store and saloon and Fister's blacksmith shop (late 1850s); the hotel burned and was rebuilt; Frank Ryan ran it as a hotel and dance hall from 1862, and in 1867 the Catholic congregation bought it and used it as a church. By 1884 'business of all kinds has entirely deserted this part of the township'.
